errors.network: The server could not be reached.

widget.unreachable: The service could not be reached.
widget.timeout: The service did not answer in time.
widget.no_integration: This widget needs a connection to a service.
widget.http_error: The service answered with an error.
widget.not_json: The service did not answer with data; probably a login page.
widget.missing_location: A place or coordinates are missing.
widget.place_not_found: The place could not be found.
widget.no_stream: This widget has no live video.
widget.too_many_streams: The server relays only a limited number of live streams at once.
widget.no_channel: There is no camera with this channel number.
widget.device_error: The device answered with an error.
widget.not_ready: The service has not been set up yet.
widget.nexmail_key_missing: nexmail received no API key. Enter the key in this connection.
widget.nexmail_key_invalid: nexmail does not know this key, or it was revoked. Create a new key in nexmail under Settings → API keys and enter it in this connection.
widget.nexmail_keys_off: API keys are turned off on this nexmail installation. The operator of nexmail turns them on under Settings → API keys.
widget.nexmail_counts_only: This key may only read counts. Edit it in nexmail and choose “Count, sender and subject” to see the latest mail.
widget.nexmail_mailbox_unknown: A mailbox picked on this card is no longer shared with this key. Pick the mailboxes again in the card's settings, or share the mailbox on the key in nexmail.
widget.nexmail_bad_limit: nexmail refused the number of messages. Pick between 1 and 20.
widget.nexpulse_key_invalid: nexpulse does not know this API key, or it was revoked. Create a key in nexpulse under Settings → API keys and enter it in this connection.
widget.nexpulse_read_only: This API key may only read. Create a key with “Read and start tests” in nexpulse to start a test from nexdeck.
widget.nexpulse_busy: nexpulse is already running a test. The card shows it as soon as it is done.
widget.nexpulse_source_off: This source is turned off in nexpulse. Turn it on there, or pick another source in the card's settings.
widget.nexpulse_source_unknown: nexpulse does not know this source. Pick another one in the card's settings.
widget.nexpulse_bad_range: nexpulse does not know this period. Pick another one in the card's settings.
widget.nextrmnl_key_missing: nextrmnl received no API key. Enter the key in this connection.
widget.nextrmnl_key_invalid: nextrmnl does not know this key, it was deleted, or the account that made it is no operator any more. Create a new key in nextrmnl under Settings → Security → API keys.
widget.nextrmnl_keys_off: API keys are switched off on this nextrmnl. The operator switches them on under Settings → Security → API keys.
widget.nextrmnl_too_old: This nextrmnl has no API for dashboards yet. It needs a version with API keys.
widget.readmeabook_not_admin: This token belongs to a user, not an administrator, and ReadMeABook shows its figures only to administrators. Create a token while signed in as an administrator.
widget.readmeabook_too_old: This ReadMeABook does not let API tokens read its figures. It needs version 1.2.0 or newer.
widget.nginxignition_stats_unsupported: This nginx build does not support traffic statistics.
widget.nginxignition_stats_disabled: Traffic statistics are disabled in settings.
widget.nginxignition_stats_stopped: Traffic statistics require nginx to be running.
widget.nginxignition_stats_unavailable: nginx ignition could not read the traffic statistics of nginx.

auth.wrong: User name or password is wrong.
auth.throttled: Too many attempts. Wait a few minutes.

forgot.lead: Enter your user name or your e-mail address. If there is an account with an address on file, a link goes out.
forgot.sent: If there is an account with an address on file, a link is on its way. It is good for 30 minutes.

twoFactor.askCode: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.askRecovery: Enter one of your recovery codes.

reset.done: The password is set. Every browser and every API token of the account was signed out.
reset.stale: This link is used up or too old. Ask for a new one on the sign-in page.

home.why: This browser is on the home network.

intro.0: The first account is the administrator. Everything else can be changed later.
intro.1: Both can be changed any time in the profile.
intro.2: The demo fills a board with invented, moving data so you see what nexdeck can do. A real Docker host gives you your containers right away.

demo.label: Start with a demo board
demo.help: Every integration runs in demo mode with fake data. Switch it off later under System > Integrations.

docker.label: Connect a Docker host
docker.help: Containers become tiles, and their state, CPU and memory appear live.
docker.hostHelp: Mount /var/run/docker.sock into the container, or use tcp://host:2375.

setup.passwordShort: At least eight characters: {{missing}} more to go.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.help: How nexdeck itself sends mail: password resets and other messages that have to go out before anyone is signed in. Notification channels keep their own server.
mail.hostHelp: Empty means nexdeck sends no mail at all.
mail.usernameHelp: Leave empty for a server that needs no sign-in.
mail.fromAddressHelp: The address recipients see, and often the one the server insists on.
mail.testHelp: Sends one mail through the settings above, so a wrong password shows up here and not at the moment someone is locked out.
mail.notConfigured: Enter an SMTP server and save it first.

profile.title: Profile
profile.pictureHelp: Shown in the bar at the top and wherever your name appears. PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 2 MB.
profile.emailHelp: Only for a forgotten password. Nothing else is sent to it.
profile.barLanguagesHelp: The two buttons next to the appearance. The language you use is always one of them.
profile.barFirst: First language in the top bar
profile.barSecond: Second language in the top bar
profile.passwordHelp: Changing it signs out every other session of this account.
profile.passwordChangedSignIn: Password changed. Every session of this account has ended; signing you in again.
profile.factorRequiredHere: This installation asks every account for a second factor. Set one up below to carry on.
profile.sessionsHelp: Every browser that is signed in with this account.
profile.tiltHelp: Only with a mouse, and never when the system asks for less motion.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.help: One integration is one connection to a service. Widgets pick from them.
integrations.addHelp: Pick the service. You can test the connection before saving.
integrations.removeBody: {{count}} widgets use it. They stay and show that they need a connection.
integrations.betaHelp: This adapter has not been confirmed against a live instance yet. If something looks wrong, please report it.
integrations.name: Name
integrations.demoHelp: Fake, moving data instead of the real service.
integrations.adminOnlyHelp: Only administrators build cards on this connection. Users still see its cards on a board that was shared with them, and it stays out of their list.
integrations.notifyHelp: Notices on. Click to mute this connection: nothing about it reaches the bell or a channel.
integrations.mutedHelp: Muted: nothing about this connection reaches the bell or a channel. Its cards keep running. Click to turn notices back on.
integrations.bellFailed: The notices could not be switched.

version.notAskedHelp: Switch on Check for updates under System, About to compare with the newest release on GitHub.

users.title: Users
users.help: Administrators manage everything. Users own boards. Guests only look.

channels.title: Notification channels
channels.help: Where outages, recoveries and failed actions are sent.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.help: A token reads what your account may see or, with full access, does everything your account may. Use it in scripts and automations.
tokens.created: This is your token. It is shown only once.
tokens.name: Token name
tokens.scopeHelp: A read-only token can look but never change anything: every request other than reading is refused. Give full access only to a script that has to change something.

boards.title: Boards
boards.help: Every board you may open, with your permission.
boards.provisioning: Files in data/boards/*.yaml become boards on their own and are edited in the file.

system.title: System
system.installationHelp: Settings that concern the whole installation.
system.publicUrlHelp: As browsers see nexdeck. Needed for identity providers and Web Push.
system.demoHelp: Every widget shows fake data. Switch it off when you connect real services.
system.demoForced: Set by NEXDECK_DEMO on the container. Remove the variable and restart to switch it off.
system.updateCheckHelp: Asks GitHub once a day whether a newer nexdeck exists, and every six hours for the newest releases of your connected services. Off by default.

search.title: Search that leaves the house
search.help: The bar behind Ctrl+K finds boards, cards and settings. This is where a typed word may go besides: to a search engine, or to a service that is already connected.
search.enabledHelp: Off means the bar stays inside nexdeck.
search.name: Name
search.empty: No target yet. Without one the bar stays inside nexdeck.
search.hint: A shortcut in front jumps straight there: !y for YouTube.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.help: nexdeck ships one look in two brightnesses. Here you set the accent colour for everyone, and you may add a style sheet of your own.
appearance.accentHelp: Applies to every account and both brightnesses.
appearance.ownHelp: Left empty, the colour chosen above wins.
appearance.cssHelp: Loaded on every page, after everything nexdeck ships.
appearance.cssLimits: At most 20,000 characters. @import is not allowed: it would fetch a file from somewhere else.
appearance.reset: Back to what it shipped with
appearance.previewHelp: This is what buttons, marks and highlights look like with it.
appearance.themeHelp: The colours of the whole interface, for dark and for light. The brightness switch keeps working: a theme brings both.
appearance.themeWeak: Some colours of this theme are hard to read, below a contrast of 4.5:1:
appearance.themeShare: Paste a theme or take this one along
appearance.themeShareHelp: A theme is a name and the colours for dark and light as #rrggbb, in JSON. Colours left out stay as nexdeck has them.

themePaste.shape: A theme needs a name and the colours for dark, for light, or both.

appearance.themeAccent: The theme brings its own accent for dark and for light. A colour of your own below still wins.
appearance.loadFailed: The look could not be read from the server.
appearance.cardsHelp: How every card is drawn, for everyone. A red or amber frame stays in every style.
appearance.looksHelp: Theme and cards that go together, in one click. Shown at once; saved with the button.
appearance.lookShareHelp: The theme, a colour of your own and the cards as a short text: copy it here and paste it into another nexdeck. Your own style sheet stays out, it is code.
appearance.refractionHelp: The rim of the glass bends what lies behind it. It costs some graphics power; switch it off for an old wall tablet.
appearance.refractionNotHere: This browser cannot do it: Chrome and Edge can, Safari and Firefox show the glass without the bend.

journal.title: Log level
journal.intro: How much nexdeck writes down. A deeper level takes effect at once, without a restart, and switches itself off again.
journal.fixedByEnv: Set through NEXDECK_LOG_LEVEL and not changed here.
journal.durationHelp: A deep level writes a lot. This is when it goes back to normal.
journal.linesIntro: The newest lines first. The short code in the fourth column is the request a line belongs to.
journal.searchPlaceholder: A word, a service, a card
journal.empty: Nothing to show. Nothing has been written at this level yet.
journal.clearBody: Every line kept, including the older files, is removed. This cannot be undone.

twoFactor.title: Second factor
twoFactor.help: A six-digit code from an app on your phone, on top of the password.
twoFactor.off: This account signs in with the password alone.
twoFactor.demanded: This installation requires a second factor, so it cannot be switched off here.
twoFactor.demandedOff: This installation requires a second factor. Set one up to carry on.
twoFactor.scan: Scan this with an authenticator app, then type the code it shows.
twoFactor.codesLead: Write these down now. They are shown once and never again, and each one works a single time.

security.title: Security
security.help: Rules that apply to every account on this installation.
security.requireTwoFactor: Require a second factor from everybody
security.requireTwoFactorHelp: Accounts with a password and without a second factor are asked to set one up and cannot switch it off again. Kiosk links are untouched: a wall display has nobody to type a code. The API tokens of such an account wait until it has one.

media.title: Media
media.help: Every picture, icon and background you have uploaded, and what still shows it.
media.removeHelp: Nothing shows this file. Deleting it cannot be undone.
media.stillUsed: This file is still shown by: {{names}}. They will show a placeholder afterwards, and this cannot be undone.

player.showHelp: While a player card is out of sight. Kept in this browser, so a phone and a desktop can each have their own.
player.headerHint: On a phone and on a wall display there is no room in the top bar; the floating bar stands in there.
player.cornerHelp: The bar can also be dragged into a corner.
player.collapsedHelp: Covers least; a click opens it again.
player.qualityHelp: Less than the original saves data on the way. When the line keeps stalling, the player turns it down by itself.

home.title: Signed in at home
home.help: A browser on the home network is signed in as one ordinary account without a password, for a wall tablet. Everywhere else the sign-in page stays, and the session opened this way counts only at home.
home.seenNone: nexdeck cannot tell your real address, so nobody is signed in automatically.
home.enabled: Sign in on the home network without a password
home.enabledHelp: Signing out on purpose holds it off in that browser for twelve hours.
home.networksHelp: One per line, like 192.168.1.0/24. Private ranges only. App tiles set to open their address automatically use them too, even with the sign-in switched off.
home.accountHelp: Never an administrator. This account cannot set a password, an e-mail address, a second factor, API tokens or kiosk links from the tablet.
home.noProxies: No reverse proxy is named in NEXDECK_TRUSTED_PROXIES. Behind a proxy, name it there, or nobody is signed in automatically.
home.saved: Saved. Sessions opened at home under the old setting have ended.

how.off: Signing in on the home network is switched off.
how.outside: This address is outside the home networks.
how.direct: Seen directly, without a proxy in between.
how.via_proxy: Seen through a proxy named in NEXDECK_TRUSTED_PROXIES.
how.forwarded_by_unknown: Something in front of nexdeck forwards this request for somebody else and is not named in NEXDECK_TRUSTED_PROXIES, so the real address is unknown.
how.proxy_without_forwarding: The proxy in front of nexdeck says nothing about whom it forwards for.
how.unreadable_forwarding: The proxy's forwarding header could not be read.
how.no_account: The chosen account is missing, disabled or an administrator.
how.factor_required: Every account owes a second factor on this installation.

brand.title: Name and logo
brand.help: Your own name and logo where nexdeck's stand: the browser tab, the bar, the sign-in page, the installed app and wall displays. "About nexdeck" keeps saying nexdeck. The sign-in page shows both, so anyone who reaches this address sees them.
brand.name: Name
brand.nameHelp: Up to 40 characters. Empty means nexdeck.
brand.logoHelp: SVG, PNG or WebP up to 512 KB. An SVG that carries script is refused. The icons of the installed app are drawn from it.
brand.removed: The logo is gone; nexdeck's mark is back.
brand.unreadable: This browser cannot draw that file. Try a PNG.
brand.appIcon_logo: From the logo, on a dark ground
brand.appIconHelp: A phone that already has the app keeps the old icon until the app is added again.
brand.boardInTitle: Put the board's name in front in the tab

report.title: Daily report
report.help: Once a day, what happened in the last 24 hours and what is still red. It goes to every channel that subscribed to "The daily report" below; nobody gets it otherwise. The time is the server's.
report.goesAt: The daily report goes out at {{time}}.
report.saved: The daily report goes out at {{time}} from now on.

addressBar.title: From the address bar
addressBar.tiles: Every app tile answers to a short name, set in its settings: {{example}} opens the tile with the short name plex, on the boards you may open.
addressBar.engines: Chrome, Edge and Firefox can add nexdeck as a search engine. A short name typed there opens its tile, other words open the search bar here with the words in it, and the address bar suggests tiles and cards while you type. Chrome and Edge list it under Settings, Search engine, Manage search engines, where it can be switched on; Firefox offers it in the menu of the address bar.
addressBar.safari: Safari cannot add search engines this way. A bookmark to a short address works there.

users.removeBody: The account goes, and it cannot be brought back.
users.setPasswordHelp: Set without the old one. Every session of that account is signed out afterwards, so tell them the new password.
users.removeOwns_one: {{count}} board belongs to this account ({{boards}}). Decide what happens to it.
users.removeOwns_other: {{count}} boards belong to this account ({{boards}}). Decide what happens to them.
users.removeAlso: Also on the account: {{what}}. That goes with it.
users.unlinkBody: {{account}} can no longer sign in through {{name}} until the account links again. Your password confirms it.

channels.pushHelp: Notifications reach this browser or the installed app, even when nexdeck is closed.
channels.pushOn: Web Push is on for this device.
channels.pushOff: Web Push is off for this device.
channels.pushDenied: The browser refused notifications. Allow them in the site settings.
channels.pushUnsupported: This browser does not support Web Push.
channels.emptyHint: Nothing set up for this service yet. Every service can hold several ways: one for outages, another for everything.
channels.name: Name
channels.nameHelp: Yours to pick. It tells this way apart from the others of the same service.

telegram.account: Telegram needs an account. Sign in on the phone or in the browser.
telegram.botfather: Write to @BotFather, the bot that hands out bots.
telegram.token: Send /newbot, pick a name, and copy the token it answers with into the field on the left.
telegram.chat: Write to your new bot once, then ask @userinfobot for your chat ID. A bot may not write first, so without that one message nothing arrives.

discord.server: Open the server settings of the channel that should receive the messages.
discord.webhook: Integrations, then New Webhook. Give it a name and copy the webhook URL.
discord.paste: Paste the URL on the left. Anyone holding it can post in that channel, so treat it like a password.

slack.app: Create an app in your workspace at api.slack.com/apps.
slack.webhook: Turn on Incoming Webhooks, add one for a channel and copy its URL.
slack.paste: Paste the URL on the left.

ntfy.server: Use ntfy.sh or your own server; the address goes in the field on the left.
ntfy.topic: Pick a topic name. Anyone who knows it can read along on a public server, so make it long and unguessable.
ntfy.subscribe: Subscribe to the topic in the ntfy app, then send the test message.

gotify.server: Enter the address of your Gotify server on the left.
gotify.app: In Gotify, open Apps and create one for nexdeck.
gotify.token: Copy the application token and paste it on the left.

apprise.urls: Apprise speaks to a hundred services through one URL each. The wiki lists the format for every one of them.
apprise.paste: Paste one URL per line on the left. All of them get every message that goes this way.

email.server: This is a channel of its own, with its own SMTP server; the one under System is for password resets.
email.addresses: From address and to address are both needed. Many providers refuse a from address that is not their own.

board.demo: Demo mode: every card shows invented data, also for connections you added yourself.

none.title: No board yet
none.body: Create one and it appears here.
none.guest: Guests see the boards that are shared with them. Ask an administrator to share one.

board.saveFailed: The layout could not be saved.
board.loadFailed: The board could not be loaded.

empty.title: An empty page
empty.readonly: Nothing has been placed here yet.

board.pageNameFirst: Give the page a name first.
board.inMenuHelp: Only boards with this tick stand in the menu at the top. The others keep their place in this list and their address.
board.showAll: Show every board of this installation
board.removeBody: Its {{count}} cards go with it, along with their history and kiosk links. This cannot be undone.
board.name: Name
board.uploadHelp: PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 12 MB. Stays on this server.
board.sharingHelp: The owner and administrators always have every right.
board.kioskHelp: A kiosk link opens the board without sign-in: for a wall tablet or a TV.
board.kioskCreated: Open this address on the display. It is shown only once.
board.kioskAllowHelp: Anyone at the display can then restart containers or switch scenes.
board.fileHelp: A board is a YAML file: export it, keep it in Git, import it elsewhere. Secrets are never written out.
board.editYamlHelp: The board as text. A page or card that keeps its id stays the same card, with its check and its history; one without an id is new, and one you remove is deleted. Connections are matched by name.
board.importHelp: Paste the YAML of an exported board.
board.deleteBody: Every page and widget on it goes with it.
board.previewHint: The board shows the change right away. Save keeps it, closing the sheet discards it.
board.autoCompactHelp: Off: cards stay where you drop them, gaps are allowed and no card ever moves on its own. On: everything moves up to fill space, and cards make room while you drag.
board.editHint: Drag a card to move it. Drag the corner at the bottom right to resize it.
board.deletePageEmpty: The page is empty; nothing is lost.
board.deletePageBody: Its {{count}} cards go with it, including their history.
board.lastPage: A board keeps at least one page.
board.moveWith: Move {{name}} with the arrow keys, resize with Shift and an arrow
board.chooseBeforeAction: This needs a choice before it runs.
board.stackedHint: On a narrow screen the cards follow the order of the wide board. To move them, open the board on a wider screen.
board.columnsHelp: More columns allow finer sizes. Cards keep their place and width on the new grid; where fewer columns would put two cards on top of each other, the lower one moves down.
board.columnsShrink: Fewer columns round the widths of the cards. Save to apply.
board.fitHeight: Fit the height to the window
board.fitHeightHelp: The rows grow or shrink until the page fits the window without scrolling. A page too long for that keeps its usual rows and scrolls. Not on phones.
board.demoData: Some connections are still in demo mode and show invented data.
board.livingHelp: The last three move, slowly. With less motion asked for in the system they hold still.
board.kioskRestHelp: Without a touch for this long, the display shows the time, the weather and what is down, large on black, and moves it a little every minute so nothing burns in. A touch brings the board back.
board.cardStyleHelp: This board's cards in a style of their own, for a wall display or a board with a picture behind it.

remove.title: Remove this widget?
remove.failed: The widget could not be removed. Is the server reachable?

widget.title: Title
widget.iconHelp: Type a service name and matching logos appear below. Or lucide:name for a symbol, or an image address.
widget.linkHelp: Where the card leads when clicked. Empty uses the service address.
widget.integrationFollowHelp: Address, icon and reachability check follow the integration. Change its address once and every tile follows.
widget.linkFollows: Empty: the address of the integration.
widget.refreshHelp: How often the server asks the service. Empty uses the widget's default of {{seconds}} seconds.

health.help: The dot on the tile shows whether the address answers.
health.kindHelp: HTTP asks the service's own address and counts any answer as reachable, a login page included. TCP only checks that the port is open. Ping reaches the machine, not the service.

widget.previewHint: Every change shows on the card right away. Save keeps it, closing the sheet discards it.
widget.iconSearchFailed: The logo index could not be loaded. Try again in a moment.
widget.betaHelp: This adapter has not been confirmed against a live instance yet. If something looks wrong, please report it.
widget.timezoneUnknown: This zone is not in the browser's list. Check the spelling.
widget.showFindingsHelp: On: the card carries the reason and the warning colour. Off, which is how a new card starts: neither, so the colour on the boards means something when it does appear.
widget.pageHelp: Puts the card on another page of this board. Leave it to keep the card here.
widget.noSources: No connection of a suitable kind is set up yet.

rows.none: The card has no entries to pick from right now.

choices.pickConnection: Pick a connection first, then this fills.
choices.none: This connection offers nothing to pick here.

widget.iconUploadHelp: PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, GIF or AVIF. The file stays on this server; nothing is fetched from outside for it.
widget.iconRemoveHelp: Cards still using this file will show a placeholder. It cannot be undone.
widget.pictureBadAddress: That is not an address a picture can be loaded from.
widget.pictureLibraryEmpty: Nothing uploaded yet. Upload a file first.

app.label: App from the catalog
app.help: Name, icon, address and reachability check come from the app. Change it once under System, Apps and every tile follows.
app.auto: Automatically, at home or on the road
app.autoHelp: Automatically opens the home address in the home networks and the other one everywhere else.
app.saveAsHelp: Puts this tile into the catalog, so any board can use it. The tile follows it from then on.
app.titleHelp: Empty: the name of the app.
app.linkFollows: Empty: the address of the app. An address here wins over it.
app.aliasHelp: Opens this tile from the address bar: {{address}}. Empty takes it from the name. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.

look.title: Colour
look.ownHex: A colour of your own as #rrggbb
look.help: The colours from the list follow the theme and light or dark. A colour of your own stays as it is. A card that is down keeps its red frame.

library.title: Add a widget
library.noIntegration: There is no integration for this service yet.

notices.title: Notices
notices.deleteAllBody: All {{count}} notices go, the unread ones too. This cannot be undone.

kiosk.invalid: This kiosk link is not valid any more.

about.tagline: The live dashboard for your homelab: every service on one board, with the numbers that matter and the buttons that act.
about.askFailed: GitHub did not answer. Nothing said about the newest version.
about.thanksIntro: nexdeck is built on other people's work. Some of the following is politeness, some of it is their terms.
about.forerunnersNote: Homarr, Homepage and Glance showed what a homelab dashboard can be. nexdeck went its own way, and it started from theirs.
about.iconsNote: Dashboard Icons holds the logos of the services, Lucide the drawn symbols. Both come through the server, so no browser talks to a content network.
about.weatherNote: The weather widget asks Open-Meteo, free and without an account. Their data comes from national weather services.
about.services: Plex, Jellyfin, Emby, Radarr, Sonarr, Home Assistant and the others
about.servicesNote: nexdeck reads their APIs. The names and logos belong to them, and none of these projects has anything to do with nexdeck.
about.notifyNote: Where nexdeck writes when something happens. Apprise alone speaks to a hundred more.
about.familyNote: Nexview asks for films and series, nexmail is the mail client, nexpulse measures the line, nexcrate fetches films, series and music, nexbeat finds music, nextrmnl opens SSH and SFTP in the browser, and nexdeck watches the machines they run on.

card.noSelfFrame: This card cannot show nexdeck itself
card.liveUnsupported: Live video needs a newer browser; showing snapshots.
card.liveFailed: Live video stopped; showing snapshots and retrying.

bars.30d: Availability of the last 30 days, one bar per day
bars.7d: Availability of the last 7 days, one bar per 6 hours
bars.24h: Availability of the last 24 hours, one bar per 30 minutes
bars.6h: Availability of the last 6 hours, one bar per 7.5 minutes
bars.1h: Availability of the last hour, one bar per minute
bars.live: The last 48 checks, one bar each

search.label: Search
search.notSetUp: No search target is set up yet.

card.noButtons: No buttons yet. Add one in the widget settings.
card.buttonNotAllowed: You may look at this board, not act on it.
card.buttonNowhere: This button has no valid target.
card.noPictures: No pictures yet. Add one in the widget settings.
card.buttonWhileEditing: This button leads nowhere while you are arranging the board.

ask.noField: This card has nothing to fill in.
ask.notAllowed: You may not start anything from this board.

note.conflict: This note was changed elsewhere while you were typing.
note.tickConflict: This note was changed elsewhere; here is how it stands now.

card.collectingLong: Collecting. The first hours appear after an hour, the first days after midnight.

player.title: Music
player.failed: That did not play. The media server did not deliver.
player.lookOnly: Playing needs the right to act on this board.
player.reduced: The line was too slow; playing at 320 kbit/s for now.

lists.addAll: Add all of these to a playlist
lists.deleteBody: The playlist disappears from the media server too. Its tracks stay in the library.
lists.smartHint: The media server fills this playlist by itself; it cannot be changed here.
lists.noEditable: No playlist to add to yet. Give a new one a name above.
lists.failed: The media server did not take the change.

player.collapse: Fold the player into a round button

plex.help: Fills the token and your server's address; nothing to copy.
plex.waiting: Waiting for the sign-in at plex.tv…
plex.timeout: Plex did not confirm the sign-in in time. Try again.
plex.pickServer: Local addresses come first; pick another one if nexdeck cannot reach it.
plex.noServers: This account has no Plex server of its own.

backups.title: Backups
backups.help: A copy beside the database is a restore point. It becomes a backup when it leaves this machine.
backups.makeLead: Writes a copy of the database and the loose files onto this machine. It takes a moment on a grown installation.
backups.noteHelp: What this state is, for the day you have to pick one. Optional.
backups.listHelp: The last {{count}} automatic ones are kept. Backups you wrote yourself are never swept.
backups.emptyBody: Write one before anything risky, and download it afterwards.
backups.dropBody: The copy and the files that belong to it go for good.

download.title: Download the backup
download.lead: The archive carries secret.key, so it hands over every service credential of this installation. Pick a password you would use for that.
download.lost: Without this password the archive cannot be opened again, not by us either.

restore.title: Put a backup back
restore.lead: Upload the archive and its password. Nothing is changed until you have seen what is in it.
restore.warning: This replaces the database, the key and the pictures. Everyone is signed out, you included. The current state is backed up first.
restore.withoutSafetyCopy: Restore even if the safety copy of the current state cannot be written. Only when that copy is the thing that is broken.
restore.keyOnlyFromEnv: There is no key in this archive. This installation takes its key from NEXDECK_SECRET_KEY, so the credentials will be readable if the variable holds the same value as on the machine the backup came from.
restore.noKeyAtAll: There is no key in this archive and none in the environment here. nexdeck will make a new one, and no stored credential will be readable afterwards. Every connection would have to be entered again.
restore.envKeyWins: This archive brings a key, but NEXDECK_SECRET_KEY is set here and wins. The credentials stay unreadable unless the variable holds the same value.

arrange.nowhere: No other page to go to. Add a page or a board first.
arrange.selected_other: {{count}} cards selected. Drag one or use the arrow keys to move them together; Escape lets go.
arrange.closeGapsTitle: Close gaps: every card moves up as far as it can, columns stay as they are

templates.title: Start from a template
templates.help: A ready-made board for a corner of the lab. Each slot takes any of the services it names; one left out takes its cards along, and only the holes they leave close.
templates.name: Name of the new board

imports.title: From Homepage or Homarr
imports.help: Paste or pick the files of the dashboard you use now. You see what would be made before anything is.
imports.servicesHelp: Every group becomes a section or a page, as you choose next. A service with a widget nexdeck knows becomes a connection and a card, any other a tile.
imports.homarrHelp: Homarr up to 0.15 keeps a board in data/configs. Homarr 1.0 and later keep boards in a database, which this cannot read.
imports.name: Name of the new board
imports.arrangementHelp: Sections keep everything on one screen, each group under a heading, as the other dashboard showed them. Pages show one group at a time.
imports.stillMissing: Fill in what is missing, or leave the connection out.

nexcrate.pairingText: Open nexcrate. At the top of every page it now says “nexdeck would like to connect”. Compare the code and confirm.
nexcrate.pairingDone: Paired. The key is in the field; save the connection.
nexcrate.pairingDenied: Declined in nexcrate. No key was made.
nexcrate.pairingExpired: The request ran out before a key arrived. Start it again.

demoLeave.title: Leave demo mode
demoLeave.intro: Demo mode goes off, and what the demo invented goes with it.
demoLeave.boards: Boards that were nothing but the demo go as a whole: {{names}}.
demoLeave.switched: Kept, and back to real data: {{names}}.
demoLeave.kept: Your own boards, cards and connections stay. If no board is left, a new starting board is made.
demoLeave.nothing: The demo invented nothing here; only the switch goes off.

showcase.media: Hide film and music titles too
showcase.offTitle: Showcase mode is on: names and addresses are made up. Press to switch it off.

picture.help: Drawn in this browser at twice the size, ready for a forum or a chat. Nothing is sent anywhere.
picture.showcaseHelp: Showcase mode for this picture only.
picture.failed: The picture could not be drawn.

keyFactor.text: Works only once you set up a second factor.

apps.title: Apps
apps.lead: Set an app up once and place it as a tile on any board. Change an address here and every tile follows.
apps.none: No apps yet. Add one here, or save an app tile as an app from its settings.
apps.deleteBody_one: {{count}} tile follows it. It stays, as a tile of its own with the name, icon and address it shows now.
apps.deleteBody_other: {{count}} tiles follow it. They stay, as tiles of their own with the name, icon and address they show now.
apps.name: Name
apps.addressesHelp: One for each way the app is reached, for example through the proxy, over Tailscale or directly by address and port.
apps.label: Label of address {{number}}
apps.automaticHelp: With one of the two set, a tile can open its address automatically: the one for home in the home networks named under System, Home network, and the other one everywhere else.

topology.kindCardsHelp: The usual page: cards on a grid.
topology.kindTopologyHelp: Your UniFi network as a plan, with the traffic on every link.
topology.startAll: Every network device, as a tree
topology.startAllHelp: Gateway, switches and access points with their links. Clients are added one by one afterwards.
topology.startEmptyHelp: Only the gateway. Everything else waits under Found until you place it.
topology.foundHelp: Network devices UniFi knows that are not on this page
topology.foundNone: Nothing new. Everything UniFi knows is on the plan or put away.
topology.placeHelp: Placing a device puts it under the one it hangs on, with its link and port. Nothing else on the plan moves.
topology.clientsHelp: Wired clients from UniFi, by the device they hang on. Port and traffic come along.
topology.wifiStays: {{count}} Wi-Fi clients stay a number on this access point.
topology.wifiStays_one: One Wi-Fi client stays a number on this access point.
topology.wifiStays_other: {{count}} Wi-Fi clients stay a number on this access point.
topology.wifiStaysAll: Wi-Fi clients stay a number on their access point.
topology.treeDone: Arranged as a tree, by the uplinks UniFi reports.
topology.removeClient: The client goes back into the client list. Nothing changes in UniFi.
topology.removeDevice: The device goes to Found and can be placed again from there. Nothing changes in UniFi.
topology.removedClient: {{name}} is back in the client list.
topology.parentMissing: {{name}} hangs on {{parent}}, which is not on the plan. Place {{parent}} first.
topology.readOnly: Only someone who may edit this board can change the plan.
topology.movedOn: Somebody else changed this page. It shows their version now.
topology.saveFailed: The arrangement could not be saved.
topology.viewHelp: For this browser only, like light and dark. Where two values would cover each other, the busier line keeps its value and the other shows it on hover.
topology.legend: Thicker and faster: more traffic, one lane per direction
topology.rhythm: {{name}} sends new values about every {{seconds}} s
topology.rhythmUnknown: how often {{name}} sends new values is still being measured
topology.sourceText: UniFi · {{device}}, {{port}}. The bytes it counted since its previous report, divided by the time between the two.
topology.phoneHint: On a phone the network is a list. The plan opens on a tablet or a computer.
topology.problemTitle: The network could not be read
